name: Board hygiene · 5 cards stuck in `doing` with no wake_at (never picked up)
description:
PM follow-up created on shift #43 (2026-11-19 18:01Z). Same pathological pattern the last three shifts kept hitting: a card holds the state `doing` but has `wake_at: null`, so the autonomy worker never considers it due. It is not "in progress" — it is frozen, and the board lies about it.

## Cards observed in this state (board `codx-junior maintenance`)
| Card id | Name | Column | Status | Wake |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ea349426-bb39-49f5-a905-ecc3c4c1c405` | Chat drafts, session attention notifications and session naming | To Do | doing | null |
| `5d7527d0-02dd-490a-ae42-81682b005a92` | Git push | Harness | doing | null |
| `0a59d3c8-a6ad-461f-8f66-a2b84778ea64` | Git credentials prompt + GitHub integration foundation | To Do | doing | null |
| `bd6a546d-3d88-483c-8d69-ac2438293498` | File find sub path | To Do | doing | null |
| `e65f98c8-608e-434c-9014-676005ed32a1` | Project search | To Do | doing | null |

## What to do (decide per card, do NOT bulk-flip blindly)
For each card, read it (`project_manager get_task`) and pick ONE:
1. **Really being worked on by a human** → leave `doing`, say who in a comment (`request_help`).
2. **Abandoned / never started** → `update_task(status="todo")` so the board stops claiming progress, and leave it in the backlog.
3. **Should be worked next** → give it a `wake_at` (`update_task(wake_at="…")`) so it actually gets picked up.

## Rule to prevent a recurrence
A card in `doing` without a `wake_at` is invisible to the autonomy worker. Every card this shift leaves in `doing` must carry either a `wake_at` or a named human owner in a comment.

## Budget note
One engine run per card at most; this is bookkeeping, not delivery. Close the task with a table: card · decision · new status · wake_at.
